meta.title: Generative models and doctoral writing practice

primary.text: How do doctoral candidates change their writing practices once generative language models enter supervision?
primary.scope: Four Flemish universities; doctoral candidates in the humanities and social sciences in their first two years; 2026 to 2029.
primary.completion_criterion: The question is answered when a typology of writing practices, built from observed supervision meetings and successive drafts, accounts for the variation found across the four sites.

method.approach: Multi-site ethnography of supervision, combined with a longitudinal corpus of drafts and their revision histories.

sources.description: Draft corpus with version histories, contributed by participating candidates
University policy documents on AI use in doctoral education, 2023-2026

method.procedure: Follow 24 candidates, six per university, for two years; observe four supervision meetings per candidate per year; collect every draft of one chapter with its version history; code revision operations and prompt-and-verify sequences; build the typology by thematic analysis; member-check the typology with participants in the third year.
validity_conditions: Candidates are followed from before their first sustained use of a generative model
Drafts come from a single chapter per candidate, so revisions are comparable
Field notes and transcripts are coded by two researchers independently
limits: The sample covers humanities and social sciences only, where drafting is solitary and text-centred
Candidates who refuse to share drafts are absent from the corpus
Observed meetings may differ from unobserved ones

results.claim: Candidates shift from sentence-level revision to prompt-and-verify cycles, and the shift is uneven across disciplines.
results.falsifier: Drafts show no change in the mix of revision operations over the first two years, and meetings contain no prompt-and-verify sequences.
results.evidence_needed: Paired drafts of the same chapter from two points in time, plus the transcripts of the meetings between them.

results.claim: A coding scheme for revision operations and prompt-and-verify sequences, with a codebook and worked examples.
results.evidence_needed: The codebook, the coded corpus and the worked examples, deposited with the project's data package.

warrant.gap_statement: Studies of generative models in doctoral writing rely on surveys of declared use, not on observed drafts or supervision talk.
evidence: Review of university AI policies in Flanders, 2026
